headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from ms-swift feeding Superset; no direct shared-channel evidence, but ms-swift can read/write files and emit API-backed outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so if its outputs are copied into Superset content or a shared workspace, instruction-like payloads could be reinterpreted. Superset only shows API access, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced; uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF ms-swift output is pasted into Superset dashboards, SQL snippets, or descriptions without sanitization
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared files or message queue
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste review step before importing ms-swift output into Superset
Store agent outputs in separate directories
Strip markdown/code fences from ms-swift outputs before reuse
Disable any auto-import path from files into Superset
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all transferred content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets, while Superset has only allowlisted network egress and no data classes listed. There is no documented shared workspace or direct leak path, so leakage is plausible only if the operator bridges them through files or pasted content.
conditions: IF sensitive ms-swift files are manually loaded into Superset
IF Superset is configured to query or display those files through a shared mount
mitigations: Keep ms-swift training artifacts out of Superset-accessible paths
Review any uploaded CSV/JSON before dashboarding
Use separate service accounts for each agent
Rotate any hub_token or sdk-token after shared handling
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the container or VM layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but modify_git_state is false; Superset exposes only API access and no write-capable shared resource is documented. A conflict exists only if both are aimed at the same mutable directory or external resource, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF Superset is connected to a mutable backend that ms-swift also edits
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Serialize any handoff through a single operator
Check file timestamps before overwriting
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate training outputs, logs, and configuration data that Superset could ingest as authoritative analytics inputs if the operator wires them together. Superset has API-driven downstream behavior, so a mistaken handoff could propagate errors across multiple work products even though direct automation is not documented.
conditions: IF Superset dashboards or jobs consume ms-swift-generated files without validation
IF ms-swift outputs are treated as ground truth for reporting
mitigations: Require human review of ms-swift outputs before ingestion
Validate schemas on every imported file
Compare outputs against a second source
Mark generated artifacts as untrusted
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates before Superset ingestion

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift explicitly handles hub_token and sdk-token and touches logs, checkpoints, and training outputs, while Superset lists no sensitive data classes or special compliance claims. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so the only clear issue is local handling of secrets by ms-swift; Superset is not cited for a specific compliance gap.
conditions: IF hub_token or sdk-token are stored in files later shared with Superset
IF regulated data is placed into ms-swift artifacts and then published through Superset
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared exports
Redact logs before publishing
Keep regulated datasets out of shared analytics paths
Review retention settings for exported artifacts
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries for both systems
